rows.t: Every two minutes the changed blocks of each disk are sent to the second site. This layer worked.
The Kubernetes objects that say which disk belongs to which claim are saved off site and rebuilt on the target.
Kubernetes binds each claim to its volume record, then the virtual machine can start. This is where the run stopped.

card.name: hub, ocp-primary, ocp-secondary
card.role: one manager and two application sites

def.what: A cluster is a set of machines that Kubernetes runs on. The hub manages. ocp-primary and ocp-secondary run the application.
def.creator: The lab team installed all three.
def.reader: Every object in this video is stored in one of these clusters.
def.where: Three separate clusters, each with its own API server.
def.analogy: A head office and two factories.

card.name: rhel9-node-001
card.role: a computer that runs inside the cluster

def.what: A virtual machine is a computer running as a process inside the cluster. Its disks live on the cluster's storage, not inside the machine.
def.creator: The virtualization layer, from a VirtualMachine object.
def.reader: Users connect to it, and Ramen protects its disks.
def.analogy: A desk in an office. The desk is in the building, the filing cabinet is in the basement.

card.name: rhel9-node-001
card.role: the machine's request for a disk

def.what: A claim is a namespaced object that says this workload needs a disk of this size. It is the only storage object the workload refers to.
def.creator: KubeVirt, or the GitOps tooling that deploys the machine.
def.reader: The pod that runs the machine, and Ramen.
def.analogy: A claim ticket at a cloakroom.

card.name: pvc-47291817-f92a-40a0-bf59-123465a72aae
card.role: the cluster-wide record of one real disk

def.what: A volume record represents one real disk. It holds the disk's ID and the name of the claim that owns it.
def.creator: The storage provisioner, when the claim is first bound.
def.reader: The claim controller, kubelet, and the storage driver.
def.where: Cluster scope, so it has no namespace.
def.analogy: The cloakroom's own ledger entry for one coat.

card.name: spec.csi.volumeHandle
card.role: the disk's ID on the storage system

def.what: The volume handle is the ID the storage driver uses to find the real disk. It names one image on one storage system.
def.creator: The storage driver, when it creates the disk.
def.reader: The storage driver, every time a pod needs the disk attached.
def.analogy: The serial number of the locker, not the name on the ticket.

card.name: persistent volume controller
card.role: matches each claim to a volume record

def.what: This Kubernetes controller decides which claim owns which volume record. It compares the claim's name, namespace and UID with the record's claim reference.
def.creator: The Kubernetes control plane.
def.reader: Anyone who reads a claim's phase.
def.analogy: The clerk who checks the name on the ticket against the name in the ledger.

card.name: 2m-vm · every two minutes
card.role: a repeated copy of each disk at the other site

def.what: Replication means the storage system sends changed blocks of every protected disk to the other site on a schedule. The copy is a real disk image, not a running machine.
def.creator: The storage driver, following the DRPolicy schedule.
def.reader: The target storage, and the DR objects that promote it.
def.where: Between the storage systems of the two clusters.
def.analogy: A photocopy of the ledger sent to the branch office every two minutes.

card.name: s3profile-ocp-primary-ocs-storagecluster
card.role: the off-site copy of the Kubernetes paperwork

def.what: A bucket where Ramen saves the Kubernetes objects that describe the disks: volume records, claims and group objects.
def.creator: The primary site's VRG, on its own schedule.
def.reader: The target site's VRG during a failover.
def.analogy: A fireproof filing cabinet across town.

card.name: gitops-vm-protection
card.role: the move order and the record of its progress

def.what: The hub object that records which cluster should run the application and which action is in progress. The console reads it.
def.creator: The Ramen hub operator, from the application placement.
def.reader: The Ramen hub operator, the console, and anyone debugging a move.

card.name: gitops-vm-protection
card.role: the site manager for one application

def.what: Ramen's per-application object on a site. It finds the claims, requests replication, restores the paperwork, and reports readiness.
def.creator: The Ramen hub operator, delivered to the site as a ManifestWork.
def.reader: The Ramen site operator and the hub.
def.analogy: The site manager at each factory.

def.what: A csi-addons object that treats several disks as one group, so they are promoted, demoted and resynced together. Its content object holds the group handle and the disk list.
def.creator: Ramen, when the DRPolicy says the storage supports grouping.
def.analogy: One shipping container instead of eight parcels, with a manifest listing what is inside.

card.name: csi-addons and the CSI driver
card.role: the translator and the crew that move the disks

def.what: csi-addons turns replication objects into storage calls. The CSI driver performs them: create, promote, change members, resync.
def.creator: The storage operator installs both.
def.reader: Ramen, through the objects it writes.
def.analogy: A translator and the warehouse crew.

card.name: Data Services · Disaster recovery
card.role: shows what the DR objects report

def.what: The web page that displays the DR objects. It reads their status. It does not measure the storage or the data.
def.creator: The OpenShift Data Foundation console plugin.
def.reader: Operators starting and watching a move.
def.analogy: The departure board at an airport. It shows what the system reports, not the weather.

card.name: phase, progression, condition
card.role: where the move is, what it is doing, and which checks pass

def.what: Phase is the current state of the move. Progression is the step inside that state. A condition is a named check with a status, reason and message.
def.creator: The Ramen hub operator writes them on the DRPC and the VRG.
def.reader: The console, the hub, and anyone debugging a move.
def.where: Status of the DRPC and the VRG.
def.analogy: A parcel: phase is which depot it is in, progression is what the depot is doing, conditions are the scan checks.

rows.t: Decides and records the recovery. Owns the DRPC and the VRG.
Translates replication objects into storage calls.
Moves, promotes and resyncs the disks.
Binds each claim to its volume record, using names and UIDs.
Starts the virtual machine only after the claim is Bound.

define.text: A label that ties several claims together so they are replicated and moved as one unit.
The policy's record of which storage classes match across the two clusters, and whether they can be grouped.
A DRPC condition meaning the last disk copy and the last paperwork upload completed. It is a past check, not a promise about the next restore.
The site where the application should normally run. A failover runs it at the other site, while the preferred site stays recorded.
The ACM object that carries a resource from the hub to a site, and reports what the site applied.
The step the DRPC is working on inside its current phase. It is where the detail lives.
A counter Kubernetes increments on every spec change. A condition only counts if it was observed at the current generation.
A volume whose claim reference names a claim but has no UID yet. Kubernetes treats it as reserved for that claim.
An annotation on the archived volume record that holds the target site's disk ID. Without it, the restore reuses the source ID.
